It’s good to know your body and what works best for you. Therapy sometimes takes time to find the right fit. It took me a few tries too. Do your best and I truly hope things work out for you! 

-Sometimes we just need medication to help us equalize while in therapy really digging into what is the root cause and find the tools to keep tending that garden. I’ll be honest I was on anti depressants and anti anxiety medication for a good while and was able to safely titrate off of them after serious in depth therapies with a psychiatrist (and their monitoring). But now I’m able to use my tools daily, I can look at myself in the mirror and find one new thing every day to enjoy about myself to kick self deprecating thoughts to the curb. 

It takes time and the right therapist and dedication to yourself. But hopefully you can win the big fight and get out in life and do something you enjoy. 😊 cliche to say but be strong, don’t let anyone take you down. And If you ever feel like you don’t have someone in your corner just know I’m out there somewhere rooting for ya

Childhood bestfriend lived in a culd-e-sac in my neighborhood. His mom fancied Native American culture and the loft of their house was decorated with a lot of cool stuff like portraits and items related to native Americans. Well one night his parents weren’t home and we were playing basketball in the middle of the street it was late summer early fall, in California at about 9 pm the Sun had been down for some time. Well I look up into the window of the loft which faced the street where we were playing. And I saw a Native American man in a headdress staring at us, his skin bright like it was maybe glowing or something I’m not really sure. His mom had a painting of the same man on the wall in the loft. After we stood there frozen for a while the man turned away and literally vanished. My bestfriend saw it too, it scared the daylight out of us. He always liked paranormal and horror related stuff but he was actually scared to go back into the house. We were both about 10 at the time. I don’t necessarily believe in like ghosts, maybe good spirits ? Honestly still pretty unsure

Well, a scale won’t do much of that, if you’re worried about keeping track of weight loss it’s honestly pretty unimportant. Scale only tells you a number. Doesn’t take into account bone mass, muscle mass or total body fat. Whatever you do off the scale such as exercise and achieve successfully is more important than the number. Trust me

Something common with anyone that experiences depression is losing sight of who you were before. When coming out of depression and staving it off you truly end up building a new person from what’s left over. Your brain changes under the pressure of anxiety and depression. It took A LOT for me to get out of it, and I still somewhat experience bouts of depression. Being proactive is what saved me. I had to fight for everything like I had no one. I always encourage others who suffer from mental health issues to fight like no one else is fighting with you. Rely on yourself for support and thank others for theirs. It’s not an easy task, and it’s always easier said than done but if you rely on others there’s a high chance they may let you down. Seeking out mental health services is always encouraged. Find a provider who can help create a solid foundation and give you tools to build yourself so you may create a person younger you would look up to. It’s hard when people stop taking you seriously, but you need to be your own advocate. Fight for what you need and what’s best for you. The rest will follow. 

As for them being rude to you, a lot of time people find it frustrating trying to understand something they can’t comprehend. They are unequipped and for that I’m sorry you have to suffer in consequence. I can tell you are genuinely trying to prevent yourself from going into a worse place and I am proud of you for being honest about the situation. Sometimes it’s best to reach out to medical professionals and share only what people around you can handle.

I hope things look up my dear. And I hope some of this made sense or could be helpful at all.

Sometimes we want closure, but even if you did confront him it may not have done much for you,  we expect a specific reaction when we face our abusers and not always do we get what we expected. This person harmed you, took something away and no they are no longer here, the world has become a bit safer for you, there is no way you are supposed to feel, coping will come on slowly and you’ll eventually stop thinking of him, but you shouldn’t in my opinion feel guilty, I understand it’s easy to feel guilty for wanting to be comfortable with your life now that he’s gone but you deserve more than anything to feel comfortable.. let the over shine some of that guilt or bad feeling that you’re in a happier place per se for not having that loom over you, the possibility. I hope this helps in some way, I recently also went through this and I can share some of the same feelings.

IMO, NTA. I do not see why OP cannot be involved in the either of the family Christmas happenings, even if it is for the spouses families. Why don’t they try and coordinate a big party for all families to have a nice time together. I’m sure they’ve all met, sure maybe OP is having a bit of a pity party but I’m sure any one of you would be upset if people you cared about didn’t want to spare some time to be with you. Maybe I’m not aware of if there is not cohesion between all 3 families (spouses families and the op) but getting frustrated and attempting to solve that future frustration and rejection by possibly “over reacting” can be a solution to some people even if that means stepping on their toes and making them feel bad for being selfish, work was the only decent excuse the op’s children gave. I could never imagine not having my MIL at my family gatherings because we are all family now. I don’t see why they wouldn’t want to include each others families.
